full_judgment:
JBM Hassan J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the continuation of Artha Execution Case No. 18 of 2011 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka on the basis of application of the respondent No.2 (Bank) being revived by order No. 8 dated 8-1-2014 which was concluded by a Solenama vide order No.7 dated 19-10-2011 (Annexure-D to the writ petition) should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect, and/or pass such other or further order of orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Relevant facts leading to issuance of the Rule Nisi are that the respondent No.2, Bank Asia Limited (the Bank) obtained a money decree amounting to Taka 1,10,50,363.01 by judgment and decree dated 19-4-2009 (decree signed on 23-4-2009). In pursuance of the said decree, the Bank filed 1st execution case No. 4 of 2010 on 3-1-2010 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka (the Adalat) claiming decretal amount of Taka 1,27,23,940.65. In the said execution proceeding both the judgment debtor (borrower) and the decree-holder (the Bank) came to a settlement by Solenama, and accordingly the execution case was disposed of on 20-1-2010. Since the judgment debtor-petitioner failed to adjust his liability as per the terms and conditions of the Solenama, the decree holder Bank filed 2nd execution case on 20-1-2011 being Artha Execution Case No. 18 of 2011. During pendency of the 2nd execution prodeeding, the judgment debtor-petitioner and the decree-holder Bank again, executed a Solenama on 18-10-2011 and accordingly filed an application on 19-10-2011 for disposing of the execution case in terms of the Solenama. After hearing and examining the witnesses, the Adalat by order dated 19-10-2011 disposed of the execution case in terms of the Solenama and treated the Solenama as part of the order. Ultimately, the payment having not been made in terms of the Solenama, the Bank filed an application on 1-12-2013 for continuation of the execution case and the Adalat by order dated 8-1-2014 directed to put up the records on the next day. Subsequently, the Adalat allowed the application by order dated 27-5-2014 and thereby restarted the execution case and proceeded for selling the mortgaged property through auction. Thereafter, the property was put on auction and by order dated 11-3-2015 the highest offer of the auction bidder, namely, Sumon Ahmed was accepted by the Adalat. At this stage, the petitioner filed this writ petition challenging the revival of the execution case and continuation of same and obtained the present Rule Nisi. 

 3. The decree-holder Bank appearing in the Rule has filed an affidavit in opposition controverting the statements as made in the writ petition. Contentions of this respondent, inter alia, are that in condition No. 7(i) of the Solenama, it was stipulated that in case of failure to pay the installments, the decree holder bank would be entitled to file an application for continuation of proceedings of the Artha Rin Execution Case No. 18 of 2011. Accordingly, when the judgment debtor failed to adjust his liability as per terms of the Solenama, the decree holder Bank filed an application on 1-12-2013 for restarting the execution case and the Adalat allowed the prayer by its order dated 27-5-2014. By filing the Solenama the judgment debtor have accepted all the terms and conditions of the Solenama and therefore, he cannot take the plea that the application for restarting the execution case is illegal since he is the party in default. 

 4. Mr Md Asiful Huq, the learned Advocate with Mr Bhabesh Chandra Ghosh, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that by disposing of the execution case finally on the basis of a Solenama, the Adalat became functus-officio and so it has no authority to reopen the said execution proceeding. Therefore, the subsequent orders passed after disposing of the execution case, were nullity in the eye of law. He further submits that the decree holder Bank, had all the remedies by filing 3rd execution case for recovery of the decretal dues, but without doing so it filed the misconceived application and the Adalat by the impugned order allowed the same which warrants interference by this Court. 

 5. In reply, Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2 (Bank) contends that the execution case was disposed of in terms of the Solenama treating the Solenama as part of the order. Clauses (f) and (i) of the said Solenama clearly provide that on failure to make the payment by the judgment-debtor (borrower), the execution will continue and therefore, there was no illegality in continuing the execution case by the Adalat. He further submits that according to Solenama the mode of payment was by 62 equal monthly installments, and thereby the payment period was for five years two months but the petitioner after paying 24 installments in two years, stopped the payment fraudulently in order to put the Bank in a limitation bar for filing the next execution case, and the Adalat on consideration of all aspects allowed the application and restarted execution proceeding. In support of submission, Mr Sikder refers to the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury vs Bangladesh Government, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139. He also contends that in disposing of the execution case on the basis of Solenama, the Adalat used the word “নিষ্পত্তি” instead of using the words “চূড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তি” as provided in section 38 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Act, 2003) and so the execution case was not disposed of finally. 

 7. It appears that the suit was decreed on contest for Taka 1,10,50,363.01. Subsequently, the Bank filed execution case No. 4 of 2010 on 3-1-2010. During pendency of the execution proceeding, the parties came to the settlement by a Solenama, and disposed of the said execution case No.04 of 2010 in accordance with the Solenama. But the terms for mode of payment having not been provided the Solenama could not be executed and so, the Bank again filed 2nd execution case on 20-1-2011 being No. 18 of 2011. During pendency of the said execution proceeding the Bank and the petitioner again executed a Solenama on 18-10-2011 pursuant to which the Adalat passed order on 19-10-2011 disposing of the execution case, in terms of Solenama treating the Solenama as part of order. In the said Solenama the parties incorporated the terms and conditions for making the payment within 62 equal monthly installments. After paying 24 monthly installments, the petitioner failed to continue payment and in the circumstances, the Bank filed an application on 1-12-2013 for continuing the execution case in terms of Solenama. The Adalat by order dated 27-5-2014 allowed the application and thereby restarted the execution case. Subsequently, the Adalat proceeded for disposing of the mortgaged property by auction and by order dated 11-3-2015 the highest bid was accepted. 

 8. At this juncture, question arises as to whether the Adalat can reopen the execution case after being disposed of by the order dated 19-10-2011. Therefore, to get the answer let us first see the Solenama dated 18-10-2011 relevant portions of which, in particular, clauses (f), (h) and (i) are as follows: 

 9. Embodying the aforesaid Solenama dated 18-10-2011 both the parties filed a joint application before the Adalat and pursuant to same, the Adalat passed the order dated 19-10-2011 by which the execution case alleged to have been disposed of. Operating portions of the said order are as follows: 

 10. On a plain reading of the order dated 19-10-2011 and the relevant clauses of the Solenama, it appears that the very order of the Adalat was passed on the basis of Solenama and the said Solenama is also a part of the order. Therefore, although the word “নিস্পত্তি” has been used in the order dated 19-10-2011, but if we read the clause (i) of the Solenama and the order i.e “সোলেনামা আদেশের একাংশ বলিয়া গণ্য করা হলো” it is clear that the execution case No. 18 of 2011 would be continued on failure to pay the installment. 

 11. Furthermore, in section 38 of the Act, 2003, the words “চূড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তি” have been used for finally disposing of the execution case on compromise, but here the word “নিষ্পত্তি” did not mean closure of the matter finally inasmuch as it referees to the contents of the Solenama which expressly provides for restarting the execution case on failure to follow the settlement terms. So much so, the word “নিষ্পত্তি” is subject to Solenama and so the case being reopened as per terms of the Solenama, there was no illegality in reopening the execution case. Moreover, the Solenama itself has provided time for making the payment by 62 months and so, unless the payment is paid completely within the time given in the Solenama the disposal order subject to Solenama, shall not get effect. 

 12. We also find that section 28 of the Act, 2003 provides time frame for filing next execution case within one year from the date of disposal of earlier execution case. Knowing fully about said provision the petitioner took time of 62 months for making payment by equal monthly installments, but subsequently after expiry of one year i.e making some installments, he stopped the payment and thereby the Bank was not in a position to file next (3rd) execution case within the given time frame of one year as per section 28 of the Act, 2003. Thus, it is apparent that the petitioner entered into the Solenama with the Bank promising to pay within five years, two months (62 installments) and accordingly filed joint application before the Court to dispose of the execution case on the basis of said Solenama and on the other hand, after passing of one year (limitation period) he stopped the payment and thereby, practicing fraud the petitioner could able to create situation in disposing of the execution proceeding. In such circumstances, even after closing of execution case the Court is always open and empowered to exercise the authority under section 57 of the Act, 2003 to reopen the execution case. This view of ours finds support in the case of Jahangir Kabir Chowdhury vs Bangladesh Government represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, reported in 22 BLC (AD) 139 relevant portions of which run follows: 

 14. Although, in accepting Solenama the Adalat used the word “নিষ্পত্তি” subject to Solenama, but since the dispute between the parties was settled by the Solenama, and the terms for making the payment was about more than five years, the Adalat could pass the order adjourning execution case in terms of the Solenama instead of using the word “নিষ্পত্তি” which would be more applicable in order to avoid further dispute as arises in this case. However, by using the words “সোলেসূত্রে নিষ্পত্তি করা হলো” the Adalat is empowered to reopen the case inasmuch as basic order is on the basis of Solenama which provides for continuation of the execution proceeding on failure to make the payment and admittedly the petitioner has failed to pay as per the Solenama. Considering this aspect, for argument sake, if the use of word “নিষ্পত্তি” is considered as an error of the Court, it can be corrected in exercise of its jurisdiction under section 57 of the Act, 2003. This view of ours finds support in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs MA Khair Bhuiyan, reported in 55 DLR (AD) 76 relevant portions which run as follows: 

 15. However, in order to avoid further dispute/confusion in disposing of the execution case on the basis of Solenama providing a time frame for making payment, the Adalat shall adjourn the proceeding in accordance with the Solenama instead of using the word “নিষ্পত্তি”.
